 J U D G M E N T
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .15,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 14.05.2023 at about 07.30 p.m., when he was driving an Auto bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AJ-1895, near bus stand Nalleekamenhalli Village, Midigeshi Hobli Madhugiri Taluk Tumkuru, a Bolero Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AG-0266 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to the accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to Madhugiri Government Hospital from where he got shifted to Tumkur Government Hospital and later shifted to Shreyas Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing Coolie and earning .25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of bolero vehicle by its driver.
The respondents, being the R.C. owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, 1st respondent did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that the petitioner shown occupation and income of the injured in the column.No.4 and 6 of the petition and also same to be proved by producing the authenticated documents such as contract license, business transaction of bank statement.
Further contended that the driver of bolero vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license and FC as on the date of alleged accident.
Further the injured had also contributed to the cause of alleged accident and was guilty of contributory negligence.
The auto was not driven within the limits of Bengaluru and the petitioner took the vehicle beyond the limits of BBMP.
Hence, the petitioner is only responsible for the incident and the petitioner contributed negligence to the cause of accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

2 5.

On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 14.05.2023 at about 07.30 p.m., near bus stand Nellekamenhalli Village,
Midigeshi Hobli Madhugiri Taluk, Bengaluru, when petitioner was driving an Auto bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AJ-1895, due to the rash and negligent driving of Bolero Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AG-0266 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove the contention of the petition, petitioner examined himself as PW.1, got examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center as PW.2 and MRO of Shreya Hospital got examined as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to 19 and closed his side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

The petitioner contended that on 14.05.2023 at about 07.30 p.m., accident occurred near Bus stand Nellekamenhalli Village, Midigeshi Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk, Bengaluru, while he was driving Auto bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AJ-1895, due to the rash and negligent driving of Bolero Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AG-0266 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Bolero Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AG-0266 by its driver, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of bolero vehicle by its driver, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove or disbelieve the case of petitioner.

In the cross examination, nothing to dispute or disbelieve the Srinivas A.G vs Thippeswamy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107345814/
3 contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of rider of offending vehicle could be elicited from the witness.
Nothing to dispute or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the accident and cause of accident could be elicited during the cross examination.

11. Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of bolero vehicle, the petitioner produced Ex.P.2 First Information statement lodged by one Sri.Govindaraju S/o Late Doddathimmappa with the police on 15.05.2023 with respect to the accident occurred on 14.05.2023.
On the basis of first information lodged, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC and U/s.187 of M.V.Act.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.

In the mahazar also,
the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of damages being caused to the offending vehicle.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages were caused to the vehicle.
The said document indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.5 is the wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by the petitioner.

The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the owner of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC and U/s.187 of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.7.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.7,
Srinivas A.G vs Thippeswamy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107345814/
4

this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Bolero Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AG- 0266 by its driver and same has resulted in injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by Shreyas Hospital, Bengaluru, which is marked at Ex.P.5.
The said document discloses that the petitioner sustained injuries and the injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner produced Ex.P6 - Discharge Summary, issued by Shreyas Hospital, Bengaluru which discloses the aspect of treatment availed by the petitioner at the hospital.
The petitionerd got examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P13 & 14.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and assessed disability of left arm at 39% and to the whole body at 13%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced medical bills for a sum of Rs.5,24,991/-marked at Ex.P.10 and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.21.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also,
nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.

So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .5,24,991/-
appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 14.05.2023 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital as he sustained injuries.
During the time of treatment, the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner produced Ex.P.6 & 16 - Discharge Summaries issued by Shreyas Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein it is mentioned that petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 15.05.2023 to 20.05.2023 i.e., for a period of 06 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 06 days to a sum of .3,000/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:
Srinivas A.G vs Thippeswamy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107345814/
5
The petitioner is the resident of Nandini Layout, Keppamma Layout, Bengaluru North, Bengaluru and he got admitted to the hospital for availing treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced Discharge Summaries marked at Ex.P.6 & 16.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses for conveyance during the period of treatment.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner contended that he was a Coolie and earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner not produced any satisfactory documents.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .25,000/- per month, as contended by him.
No materials are placed by petitioner in order to substantiate his contention pertaining to his occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the notional income of petitioner is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner considered as .16,000/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement.

The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N,
working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru and examined as PW.2.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained right femur fracture, left segmental fracture left femur, right tibia shaft fracture and left proximal tibia fracture with fracture of left forearm both bones and underwent ORIF with plate and screws for the left radius and ulna, CRIF with long PFN for the left femur, CRIF with IMIL Nail for the right femur & CRIF with IMIL nail for the right tibia and conservative treatment for the left proximal tibia and later discharged.

Further on recent examination for the purpose of assessment of disability, it was noticed that there was complains of unable to fold both knees unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and carry his job as auto driver and on examination, the petitioner has limping gait, restricted both knee movements, wasting both lower limb muscles,
restricted left forearm movements.

Further as per X-rays reveals that both femur shows united fracture with implant in situ, right leg shows united tibia fracture with implant in situ and left forearm shows united radius and ulna fracture with implaint in situ.
The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability of left arm at 39% and to the whole body at 13%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.13 & 14 i.e., clinical note and X-ray film.

The petitioner also examined Medical Record Officer at Shreyas Hospital as PW.3 and got Srinivas A.G vs Thippeswamy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107345814/
6

marked documents at Ex.P.15 to 19 i.e., authorization letter, discharge summary,
wound certificate, MLC Register extract and case sheet.
PW.2 stated in the evidence that the fractures are united and also stated that there is improvement in muscle power.
The said aspect indicates that the petitioner is having improvement in his condition.
PW.2 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do his routine activities in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 06%.

sentences.text: In order to prove age, the petitioner produced Ex.P.8 & 9 - Notarized Copy of Aadhaar Card and Driving License, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 15.06.1986.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to the age.
As per the documents furnished by petitioner, his age appears to be 37 years at the time of accident.
Accident occurred on 14.05.2023.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 37 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable is '15'.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (06% of prior annual income)= .11,520/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 15 Loss of future earnings - (.11,520/- x 15) = .1,72,800/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .1,72,800/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:-
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day- today activities as earlier.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of Srinivas A.G vs Thippeswamy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107345814/
7 future amenities.
(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
The doctor/PW.2
has opined that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant the estimate of this surgery the cost which is stated to be around .1,20,000/-.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials in order ascertain the actual expense required for future surgery.
No satisfactory materials are placed in order to substantiate the said aspect.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .30,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.

15.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Bolero Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AG-0266.
The materials on record disclose that respondent No.1 is the owner of offending vehicle and respondent No.2 is the insurer of said vehicle.

Respondent No.2 contended that the auto driven by petitioner was having no valid permit to ply in the place where the accident took place and as such, respondent No.2 Srinivas A.G vs Thippeswamy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107345814/
8 is not liable to pay the compensation.
It is pertinent to note that there is no allegation of rashness or negligence on the part of petitioner in the cause of accident.

Further,
respondent No.2 does not appear to be the insurer of the auto in order to consider that the terms of the policy have been violated.
The insurance company can be absolved from liability if there is any violation of conditions of policy of insurance.
In the present case, there appears to be no violation of policy condition by respondent No.1.
The contention of respondent No.2 that the auto has been plied in the area in which it has no permit to ply, does not sustain for consideration.
The said contention would have assumed importance if respondent No.2 is the insurer of auto and the claim is made against the auto.
As such, the contention of respondent No.2 does not sustain for consideration.
So, the respondents, being the R.C. owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .8,20,791/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Twenty Thousand Seven Hundred and Ninety One only) with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.

Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to the age.
As per the documents furnished by petitioner, his age appears to be 37 years at the time of accident.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 37 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.
Further,
respondent No.2 does not appear to be the insurer of the auto in order to consider that the terms of the policy have been violated.
The insurance company can be absolved from liability if there is any violation of conditions of policy of insurance.
In the present case, there appears to be no violation of policy condition by respondent No.1.
The contention of respondent No.2 that the auto has been plied in the area in which it has no permit to ply, does not sustain for consideration.
The said contention would have assumed importance if respondent No.2 is the insurer of auto and the claim is made against the auto.
So, the respondents, being the R.C. owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
